- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.65) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for 1–3 day forecasts.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral or negative, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to align with historical mean.
